census.fips.description: The Census Bureau's FIPS codes (ANSI/INCITS 38 and 31) for US states and counties: one row per state or state-equivalent and per county or county-equivalent, with Census's name, the USPS abbreviation, the GNIS code, Census's class and functional-status codes, and whether the code is in Census's current vintage. The two-digit state code and the five-digit county code are the keys most US government data is joined on. Built from Census's ANSI code lists (2020 vintage, the latest Census publishes), which cover the 50 states, DC, Puerto Rico, the Island Areas and the U.S. Minor Outlying Islands, and from its 2026 Gazetteer county file, which adds the nine Connecticut planning regions that replaced Connecticut's eight counties as county-equivalents in 2022. The eight counties are kept, marked as no longer current, since data from before 2022 uses them. U.S. Census Bureau data, a US Government work in the public domain; Meridian prepared this table from Census's files, and Census does not endorse it.
census.fips.name: fips

fields.description: The FIPS code, as other data carries it: two digits for a state or state-equivalent (01 for Alabama), five for a county or county-equivalent, the state's two digits and the county's three (01001 for Autauga County). Join other data on this column; it is text, so a leading zero is kept.
fields.name: code

fields.description: The code as Census prints it, which is the same as code.
fields.name: code_display

fields.description: Hierarchy level: 'state' for a state or state-equivalent (the 50 states, DC, Puerto Rico, the Island Areas and the U.S. Minor Outlying Islands), 'county' for a county or county-equivalent (parishes, boroughs, census areas, independent cities, municipios, districts, Connecticut's planning regions).
fields.name: level

fields.description: 0 for a state, 1 for a county.
fields.name: depth

fields.description: A county's state code; NULL on a state.
fields.name: parent_code

fields.description: Census's name for the state or county (Alabama, Autauga County, Doña Ana County), with its accents.
fields.name: description

fields.description: The name with its state's in front, joined with ' › ' (Alabama › Autauga County), so a county name repeated across states reads in context. A state's is its own name.
fields.name: description_full

fields.description: The two Census vintages the table was built from, such as 'ANSI 2020, Gazetteer 2026': the vintage of the ANSI state and county code lists, and of the Gazetteer county file. Read from the files' names. One value for every row.

fields.description: Which Census file the row came from: 'census_ansi' for the ANSI code lists, 'census_gazetteer' for a county only the Gazetteer lists (Connecticut's nine planning regions).
fields.name: text_source

fields.description: description_full lowercased and accent-stripped, the field the in-browser search reads.
fields.name: corpus

fields.name: state_code

fields.name: county_code

fields.name: state_abbr

fields.description: The eight-digit GNIS feature code Census lists for the state or county, the U.S. Geological Survey's Geographic Names Information System identifier (Census's STATENS, COUNTYNS or ANSICODE).
fields.name: gnis_code

fields.description: Census's class code for the county (CLASSFP): H1 an active county or equivalent, H4 a legally defined inactive or nonfunctioning one, H5 a statistical equivalent (Alaska's census areas), H6 a county or equivalent that is coextensive with an incorporated place or another legal entity, C7 an independent city. NULL on states, and on counties only the Gazetteer lists, since it carries no class.
fields.name: class_code

fields.description: Census's functional-status code for the county (FUNCSTAT), from the ANSI county list: A an active government providing primary general-purpose functions, B partially consolidated with another government, C fully consolidated, F a fictitious entity, G an active government subordinate to another unit, N a nonfunctioning legal entity, S statistical. NULL on states, and on counties only the Gazetteer lists.
fields.name: functional_status

fields.description: Whether the code is in Census's current vintage, as the Gazetteer county file decides: true for a county it lists, and for a state with a county in it; false for a county in a state it covers that it no longer lists, which is Connecticut's eight counties, replaced in 2022 by its planning regions; NULL where it does not cover the state, the Island Areas and the U.S. Minor Outlying Islands, whose codes the ANSI lists still carry.

census.naics_2017_to_2022.description: The U.S. Census Bureau's own concordance from the 2017 North American Industry Classification System to the 2022 edition, at the six-digit national industry level, for bridging data still coded to 2017, such as County Business Patterns through 2023: one row per pairing of a 2017 industry with a 2022 industry, as Census publishes it. A 2017 industry Census split appears once for each 2022 industry it went to, its title naming the piece that went there (Anthracite Mining - anthracite surface mining), and a 2022 industry formed from several 2017 industries once for each of them; Census gives no weights for apportioning counts between them. Every 2022 code is a national industry in census/naics_2022, which the run checks against the code list it builds from Census's descriptions workbook; the 2017 edition is not hosted, so the 2017 codes are checked by their shape only. Census's 2022 to 2017 file holds the same pairings, so this table serves both directions. Census's files are U.S. Government works in the public domain.

census.schedule_b.description: Schedule B, the U.S. Census Bureau's classification of exported goods: every ten-digit commodity Census publishes, with a row for each chapter, heading and subheading its codes imply and a parent for every row. Each commodity carries Census's units of quantity, SITC, end-use, agricultural, NAICS and high-technology codes. Chapter titles and commodity text are Census's; heading and subheading text is the U.S. International Trade Commission's, from the HTS revision named in hts_release. The data is credited to the U.S. Census Bureau; Census's bulk file carries no endorsement notice.
census.schedule_b.name: schedule_b

fields.description: Schedule B code, digits only: 2 (chapter), 4 (heading), 6 (subheading) or 10 (commodity) digits. Join other data on this column.
fields.name: code

fields.description: The code as Census prints it, with dots (0101.21.0000). For a chapter or heading, its digits; for a subheading, 0101.21.

A heading's or subheading's is USITC's text for that prefix in the HTS, except in chapter 98, where USITC's provisions are import ones, and where USITC gives the prefix no text: there it is the text of the one Census line under it, or, with several lines under it, a label such as 'Heading 9802'. text_source says which.

x-joins.$comment: How to join Schedule B's NAICS codes to census/naics_2022, and how far the join reaches. It is NOT a `schema.foreignKeys` entry: a foreign key asserts that every value on the left exists on the right, and some of Census's NAICS codes on Schedule B lines are not codes of the 2022 edition. `coverage` does not live in this file: `crosswalk_join.py --write` measures it from the build and writes it into the generated `datapackage.json`.

joins.cardinality: partial — 9,464 of 9,779 rows match. The unmatched lines carry a code that is not a 2022 NAICS code: an industry code ending in X (33641X, 1121XX), which Census's layout does not define and which reads, from the codes' shape, as digits left unspecified, or one of the codes 910000, 930000 and 990000, which Census gives to lines such as waste and scrap, used goods and chapter 98's special provisions.
joins.description: The NAICS industry Census assigns to each ten-digit commodity. Join `naics` to `naics.code` on commodity rows; both sides are text. Chapter, heading and subheading rows carry no NAICS code.
joins.evidence: Census's Schedule B export file (econcord.txt) prints a six-character NAICS code on every ten-digit line, at characters 266 to 271 of the layout Census publishes with it (exp-stru.txt, `NAICS classification`). Where the code is a 2022 national industry, it names that industry in census/naics_2022.
joins.name: naics

x-joins.verifiedBy: datasets/edgar_gleif/scripts/crosswalk_join.py — the same script both writes and checks `coverage`. Run with `--write`, right after `describe`, it measures the join above against this build's own Parquet and writes `coverage` into datapackage.json (arcform.yaml step `derive_join_coverage`). Run with no flags, it re-measures against the published objects instead and fails if the committed `coverage` disagrees.

cms.hcpcs.description: HCPCS Level II, the alpha-numeric codes the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) maintain for billing supplies, drugs, equipment and services that CPT does not cover: one row per code in CMS's quarterly file, current and terminated, with its long and short description, the dates CMS added, last changed and terminated it, and CMS's pricing, coverage, BETOS and type-of-service fields. Two parts of CMS's file are not CMS's own work and are left out: the American Dental Association's dental codes (the D series, CDT) and every CPT code of the American Medical Association, including CPT codes CMS cites in a cross-reference or a description; where a description cited one, the number is replaced by '[CPT code]' and text_source says so. Modifiers are not included.

fda.ndc.description: The FDA's National Drug Code directory: the codes that identify each finished drug sold in the United States, as one row per labeler, product and package, with each package under its product and each product under its labeler. Each product row carries the FDA's fields for it: brand and generic name, dosage form, routes, active ingredients and strengths, pharmacologic classes, DEA schedule, marketing category and application number, and marketing dates; each package row carries its description and dates, and its product's fields. Read from openFDA's NDC download, which the FDA releases under CC0; unfinished drugs (bulk ingredients and drugs for further processing) are not included. The FDA updates the directory daily and Meridian refreshes this dataset fortnightly, so release gives the date the data is as of. The listings are submitted by the labelers, and the FDA does not verify them: a code's presence in the directory does not mean the FDA has approved the drug. Brand names can be trademarks, which CC0 does not waive.
fda.ndc.name: ndc

fields.description: The NDC in the eleven-digit form claims and most other data carry, digits only, each of the FDA's three segments padded with zeros to 5-4-2: a package 00002015201, its product 000020152, its labeler 00002. Join other data on this column; for data that carries the FDA's hyphenated ten-digit form, join on code_display.

fields.description: The NDC as the FDA prints it, with hyphens and without padding: a package 0002-0152-01 (in one of the layouts 4-4-2, 5-3-2 or 5-4-1), its product 0002-0152, its labeler 0002.
fields.name: code_display

fields.description: Hierarchy level: labeler (the firm the FDA assigned the labeler code to), product (a drug as one labeler lists it: one strength and dosage form) or package (one package size and type of that product, the level claims carry).

A product: its brand name, suffix included, then its generic name in brackets where that differs, then its dosage form (Zepbound (tirzepatide), INJECTION, SOLUTION); the generic name alone where there is no brand name. A package: the FDA's package description (1 VIAL, SINGLE-DOSE in 1 CARTON (0002-0152-01) / .5 mL in 1 VIAL, SINGLE-DOSE).

fields.description: The labeler's name, the product's text and the package's description, joined with ' › ', down to the row's own level.
fields.name: description_full

gleif.lei.description: The Global Legal Entity Identifier Foundation's public register of legal entities — every entity with its 20-character LEI, legal name, country, jurisdiction and registration status.
gleif.lei.name: gleif

fields.description: The 20-character ISO 17442 Legal Entity Identifier — the entity's globally unique key in the GLEIF register.
fields.name: lei

fields.description: The entity's official legal name, as recorded in the GLEIF golden copy. The bounds are the register's own: LEI-CDF v3.1 types this element NameType, a complexType whose simpleContent extends Tokenized500Type — the extension adds an optional xml:lang attribute and leaves the inherited value space, which restricts the text to between 1 and 500 characters. Names at both ends are genuine — single-character names are registered in several jurisdictions, and names past 200 characters are typically a registry's full form, such as the Italian convention of carrying the permitted trading abbreviations inside the registered name. The type on this field is declared, not inferred: `nominations.finetype.json` beside this descriptor nominates `representation.text.entity_name` and says why, so the field carries `x-finetype-nominated` and no confidence. Its bounds are the register's rather than that label's, whose two to two hundred characters would refuse the genuine names at both ends. Inferred, the label is a draw: finetype returned it on 424 of 600 independent 100-value samples of this column and one of several other types on the rest.
fields.name: legal_name

fields.description: Country of the entity's legal address, as the GLEIF register records it. The register types this element as a two-letter country code (LEI-CDF v3.1's CountryCodeType), and the pattern here is that shape. It checks shape, not assignment: the schema itself notes that a well-formed pair of upper-case letters need not be a valid ISO 3166 entry, and values outside the ISO-assigned list do occur in this column, so treat membership of an ISO reference list as something to verify rather than assume.
fields.name: country

fields.description: City of the entity's legal address.
fields.name: city

fields.description: Jurisdiction the entity is constituted under, as the GLEIF register records it. The register types this element as a country code or a country-plus-subdivision code — LEI-CDF v3.1's JurisdictionCodeType, a union of its CountryCodeType and RegionCodeType — and the pattern here is the union of those two shapes. It checks shape, not assignment: the schema itself notes that a well-formed value need not be a valid ISO 3166 entry, and values outside the ISO-assigned lists do occur in this column, so treat membership of an ISO reference list as something to verify rather than assume.
fields.name: jurisdiction

fields.description: ELF (Entity Legal Form) code classifying the entity's legal form.
fields.name: legal_form

fields.description: The register's entity status, as text: ACTIVE (legally registered and operating as of the last report), INACTIVE (no longer legally registered or operating), or the four-character string NULL, which the register uses to mean the status is not applicable. These three are LEI-CDF v3.1's EntityStatusEnum. It is not a boolean, and the string NULL is a reported value rather than a missing one — the field is declared required so that an actual SQL null reads as a violation instead of as a synonym for that value.
fields.name: entity_status

fields.description: LEI registration lifecycle status (e.g. ISSUED, LAPSED, RETIRED).
fields.name: registration_status

fields.description: Date the LEI was first registered (calendar date sliced from the golden-copy timestamp).
fields.name: initial_registration

fields.description: Date the LEI registration is next due for renewal.
fields.name: next_renewal

fields.description: Lowercased, accent-stripped concatenation of legal name + city + country — a derived free-text search field, not a source attribute. The type on this field is declared, not inferred: `nominations.finetype.json` beside this descriptor nominates `representation.text.plain_text` and says why, so the field carries `x-finetype-nominated` and no confidence. Inferred, the label is a draw: finetype returned it on 377 of 600 independent 100-value samples of this column and `unknown` on 207, and the previously published `unknown` was one such draw.
fields.name: corpus

gleif.lei.title: GLEIF — Legal Entity Identifiers

library.edgar_lei.description: A resolved crosswalk linking SEC EDGAR registrants (CIK / ticker / fund series) to their GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier (LEI) — one row per link between an EDGAR identifier and an LEI, each carrying its provenance tier, method and confidence. Authoritative edges come from official SEC/GLEIF registration (no guessing); the operating-company tail is linked by probabilistic name resolution (Fellegi-Sunter / Splink): exact normalized-name matches are confirmed (~95% precision), while name-only fuzzy matches are surfaced as candidates rather than auto-confirmed. A point-in-time snapshot, with an as-of date on every row.
library.edgar_lei.name: edgar_gleif

fields.description: Scheme of the SEC identifier held in `key`, and the discriminator that says how to read that column. This snapshot carries two: cik (an EDGAR Central Index Key, rendered as decimal digits) and series (an SEC fund identifier, a letter prefix followed by digits). A third scheme, class (fund share class), is producible by the pipeline but is absent from this snapshot.
fields.name: key_type

fields.description: The SEC-side identifier this edge is keyed on, read according to `key_type`: for cik rows an EDGAR Central Index Key in decimal digits with no leading zeros; for series rows an SEC fund identifier — an uppercase letter prefix followed by digits (S…, CEF…). Text, not a number: the two schemes share one column, so the pattern above is their union and no arithmetic type describes it. To join it to `edgar.cik`, render that integer column as text — see `x-joins`.
fields.name: key

fields.description: The type on this field is declared, not inferred: `nominations.finetype.json` beside this descriptor nominates `representation.text.entity_name` and says why, so the field carries `x-finetype-nominated` and no confidence. Inferred, the label is a draw: finetype returned it on 246 of 300 independent 100-value samples of this column, and unknown on 36, plain_text on 14 and full_address on 2.
fields.name: company_name

fields.description: GLEIF Legal Entity Identifier (ISO 17442): a four-character alphanumeric LOU prefix, fourteen alphanumeric entity characters, then two check digits — ISO 7064 MOD 97-10 over the eighteen that precede them. The `pattern` below states the shape and nothing more: no regular expression evaluates a checksum, and `00000000000000000000` satisfies this one. The arithmetic is checked where the edge is built: `models/load.sql` declares it and `models/package.sql` gates the terminal table on it. A value GLEIF publishes is admitted whether or not its check digits satisfy the standard, because the register defines which identifiers exist.
fields.name: lei

fields.description: The entity's official legal name — GLEIF's own `legal_name` column, carried through the join unchanged (`models/package.sql` selects `g.legal_name`), so it is the same register element `gleif.legal_name` describes and takes the same bounds. LEI-CDF v3.1 types this element NameType, a complexType whose simpleContent extends Tokenized500Type, restricting the text to between 1 and 500 characters — the value space `gleif.legal_name`'s own description names for the same element, not a bound measured off one build. A snapshot narrower than the register at either end would be true of today's rows and false of the element a consumer is validating against.
fields.name: legal_name

fields.description: GLEIF's authoritative entity category (e.g. GENERAL, FUND, BRANCH); GENERAL when unknown.
fields.name: category

fields.description: Jurisdiction the entity is constituted under, as GLEIF records it: a country code or a country-plus-subdivision code (country, hyphen, subdivision) where GLEIF holds one — US-DE, AE-SH. It checks shape, not assignment: a well-formed value need not be a valid ISO 3166 entry, and values outside the ISO-assigned lists do occur in this column, so treat membership of an ISO reference list as something to verify rather than assume. The type on this field is declared, not inferred: `nominations.finetype.json` beside this descriptor nominates `geography.location.country_code` and says why, so the field carries `x-finetype-nominated` and no confidence. No label names the union of the two shapes, and every value begins with its country; the pattern here stays widened past that label's two letters to admit the subdivision suffix. Inferred, the label is a draw: finetype returned geography.location.state_code on 260 of 300 independent 100-value samples of this column, geography.location.country_code on 34 and unknown on 6.
fields.name: jurisdiction

fields.description: GLEIF's registration status for the matched LEI record — ISSUED, LAPSED, RETIRED or another of the register's states. The type on this field is declared, not inferred: `nominations.finetype.json` beside this descriptor nominates `representation.text.word` and says why, so the field carries `x-finetype-nominated` and no confidence. Inferred, the label is a draw: finetype returned it on 262 of 300 independent 100-value samples of this column and geography.location.state_code on 38.
fields.name: reg_status

fields.description: How the edge was established. Authoritative: sec-registration (GLEIF RA000665) or sec-ncen (SEC Form N-CEN). Probabilistic: exact_name (identical normalized company name) or jaro_winkler (fuzzy name).
fields.name: method

fields.description: Provenance tier, in precedence order: authoritative (deterministic SEC/GLEIF registration — no guessing), confirmed (exact normalized-name Splink match, ~95% precision), candidate (name-only fuzzy match, surfaced NOT asserted), ambiguous (one exact name matched more than one entity). A deterministic edge always wins over a name match for the same key. The type on this field is declared, not inferred: `nominations.finetype.json` beside this descriptor nominates `representation.text.word` and says why, so the field carries `x-finetype-nominated` and no confidence. Inferred, the label is a draw: finetype returned it on 193 of 300 independent 100-value samples of this column and datetime.component.month_name on 107.
fields.name: tier

fields.description: Edge confidence in [0, 1]: 1.0 for authoritative edges; the Fellegi-Sunter posterior match probability under the frozen resolution model for probabilistic edges.
fields.name: confidence

fields.description: The date this linkage was asserted — the vintage of the sources the edge was resolved from, stamped on every row at build time. Constant within any one published build, and that is the point: an edge carries its own vintage, so a row copied out of this table into a warehouse still says when it was true, and two builds unioned together stay tellable apart. The package's top-level `created` records when the descriptor was written, which is a different fact and does not travel with the rows. A link is a claim about two identifiers at a moment: EDGAR registrants change name and ticker (the CIK itself is permanent and never expires, per the SEC), LEIs lapse and transfer, and an edge resolved in July is not evidence about December. Read it as the as-at date for the claim, not as a modification timestamp.
fields.name: as_of

fields.description: Lowercased, accent-stripped concatenation of the display name, legal name, ticker and LEI — a derived free-text search field, not a source attribute. The type on this field is declared, not inferred: `nominations.finetype.json` beside this descriptor nominates `representation.text.plain_text` and says why, so the field carries `x-finetype-nominated` and no confidence. Inferred, the label is a draw: finetype returned it on 186 of 300 independent 100-value samples of this column, and unknown on 75, alphanumeric_id on 37 and semicolon_separated on 2.
fields.name: corpus

library.edgar_lei.title: EDGAR ↔ GLEIF — company-to-LEI crosswalk

x-joins.$comment: How to join this crosswalk to the packages it references, and how far each join reaches. These are NOT `schema.foreignKeys`: a Data Package foreign key asserts that every value on the left exists on the right, and neither of these joins satisfies that against the published bytes — see each `cardinality` and (in the built descriptor) `coverage`. Declaring them as foreign keys would advertise a guarantee the data does not keep, so the guarantee is dropped and the reachable part is stated instead. `coverage` does NOT live in this file: a hand-typed row count decays as soon as an upstream source grows, which is exactly what happened here (four weeks stale on 2026-08-13). `crosswalk_join.py --write` measures it from the build and writes it into the generated `datapackage.json` instead.

joins.cardinality: partial — 6,357 of 189,204 rows match. Neither side contains the other.
joins.description: SEC-side identity: a cik-typed edge to the EDGAR company-ticker table. `edgar` is a ticker/exchange listing, not the CIK universe, so it covers a small part of the registrants this crosswalk keys on; the direction of containment runs neither way. Join by rendering `edgar.cik` (an integer) as text and comparing it to `key` (text) — the rendering is exact, because no published CIK carries a leading zero.
joins.evidence: For key_type='cik' rows, `key` is the EDGAR Central Index Key as reported to SEC EDGAR. Where both sides hold the same registrant the values agree exactly; the shortfall is coverage, not disagreement — `edgar` is built from the SEC's company-tickers file, so its reach follows that file rather than the registrant population.
joins.name: edgar

joins.cardinality: complete — all 213,033 rows match. `coverage` is written into the built descriptor, not into this file — see `verifiedBy` below.
joins.description: GLEIF-side identity: the LEI each edge resolved to. Join `lei` to `gleif.lei` directly — both sides are text and no rendering is involved.

evidence.comparison: normalized company name (exact, then Jaro-Winkler tiers)
evidence.method: Fellegi-Sunter probabilistic record linkage (Splink), frozen model, for the operating-company tail; official SEC/GLEIF registration for authoritative edges
evidence.precision: exact normalized-name matches auto-confirmed (~95% precision, spot-checked); name-only fuzzy matches surfaced as candidate, not confirmed
evidence.tie_break: ISSUED > LAPSED > RETIRED, then US jurisdiction

joins.name: gleif

x-joins.verifiedBy: datasets/edgar_gleif/scripts/crosswalk_join.py — the same script both writes and checks `coverage`. Run with `--write`, right after `describe`, it measures each join above against this build's own Parquet and writes `coverage` into datapackage.json (arcform.yaml step `derive_join_coverage`). Run with no flags, it re-measures against the published objects instead and fails if the committed `coverage` disagrees.

library.ourairports.description: OurAirports' airports that carry an ICAO code, the four-letter code air traffic control, flight plans and airspace data use for an airport: one row per ICAO code, with OurAirports' name for the airport, its type, coordinates and elevation, its country and region codes and names, the place it serves, whether it has scheduled airline service, its GPS and local codes, and links to its website and Wikipedia article. Airports without an ICAO code are not included. IATA's three-letter airport codes are left out, since IATA's code list is not open data: OurAirports' iata_code column is not read into the table, and its keywords column is dropped because it carries IATA codes. Data from OurAirports (https://ourairports.com/), which its maintainers release to the public domain and which comes with no guarantee of accuracy; Meridian prepared this table from OurAirports' files, and OurAirports does not endorse it. The date in release is the UTC date of the commit OurAirports last made to its data repository before the run, the commit the files were read at. GitHub records a commit only when the files change; in practice airports.csv changes nightly. Meridian refreshes this dataset fortnightly, so the data is as of the date in release.

fields.description: The unit or units of quantity USITC prints for the line (for example 'kg' or 'No.'), as a list; NULL where none is printed.
fields.name: units

fields.description: The general (column 1) rate of duty. The rate is as USITC prints it, blank as NULL. A line that prints none of the general, special and column 2 rates takes all three from its nearest printed ancestor that prints a general rate, named in rate_from_code. Where no printed ancestor prints a general rate (a heading such as 0101), the three stay NULL, as they do on chapters and on rows made for prefixes USITC prints only through longer codes. Chapter 99 provisions can add duties to this line, whether or not its footnotes name them, and those duties are not included here.
fields.name: general_rate

fields.description: The special (column 1) rate of duty, with the programme codes USITC prints. The rate is as USITC prints it, blank as NULL. A line that prints none of the general, special and column 2 rates takes all three from its nearest printed ancestor that prints a general rate, named in rate_from_code. Where no printed ancestor prints a general rate (a heading such as 0101), the three stay NULL, as they do on chapters and on rows made for prefixes USITC prints only through longer codes. Chapter 99 provisions can add duties to this line, whether or not its footnotes name them, and those duties are not included here.
fields.name: special_rate

fields.description: The column 2 rate of duty. The rate is as USITC prints it, blank as NULL. A line that prints none of the general, special and column 2 rates takes all three from its nearest printed ancestor that prints a general rate, named in rate_from_code. Where no printed ancestor prints a general rate (a heading such as 0101), the three stay NULL, as they do on chapters and on rows made for prefixes USITC prints only through longer codes. Chapter 99 provisions can add duties to this line, whether or not its footnotes name them, and those duties are not included here.
fields.name: column2_rate

fields.description: The code of the printed line whose rates this row carries: the row's own code where it prints a rate, otherwise its nearest printed ancestor that prints a general rate. Join on this to find the rate that applies to a ten-digit import code. NULL on chapters, on every row made for a prefix USITC prints only through longer codes, and on a printed line that prints no rate and has no printed ancestor that prints a general rate.
fields.name: rate_from_code

fields.description: The footnote texts USITC prints for the line, as a list. Some name chapter 99 provisions that can add duties to the line.
fields.name: footnotes

fields.description: USITC's quota quantity field, as printed. USITC leaves it empty on every row of the current revision, so the column is NULL throughout.
fields.name: quota_quantity

fields.description: The additional-duty text USITC prints on chapter 99 provision lines (for example 'No additional duty'), as printed. NULL where USITC leaves it blank, including rows that hold only a space.
fields.name: additional_duties
